title: When Sixty Women Waited, the Hamlins Built a Hospital of Their Own
conflicts: Opening date: 1974 per Catherine Hamlin (ABC 2008, Right Livelihood speech), the Guardian, the BBC and the charity's 2015 founders page; 24 May 1975 per the Embryo Project (ASU). The story uses the founder's 1974 and notes 1975. Patient totals differ by date and scope (30,000 in 2008 per Catherine; 43,000 in 2015 per the charity; 30,000+ by 2015 at the Addis hospital per Embryo Project; 60,000+ by 2020 per the Guardian and BBC, including regional hospitals); the story gives the 2020 figure with the BBC's 'thought to have' hedge and says it covers the network. A single-source GBP 10,000 New Zealand donation (Embryo Project) was left out.
notes: Company is set to 'Hamlin Fistula Ethiopia' because 'Addis Ababa Fistula Hospital' shares the word 'hospital' with the Aravind edition (1976) and the repeat screen blocked it; the hospital is named in the story. Two key sources (ABC Talking Heads transcript, hamlinfistula.org founders page) are Internet Archive copies. Quote stance: affirms.
